the_blocking_finding_is_false.why_no_existing_check_catches_it: F06 carries fact_ids: [] and absent: [] (both empty). scope_defect()'s chain (src/repository_presenter/components/readme/review/independent/review.py) runs absence_defect() first (line 408) - it returns None immediately when _claimed_absent(finding) is empty (line 442-443), never checking the candidate's own bytes. Because criterion == 'presentation', the chain then reaches cited_fact_defect() (line 320) - it also returns None immediately when finding.get('fact_ids', []) resolves to no product facts (line 350-353), by the same design factuality_defect() uses. factuality_defect() (line 238) already closes this exact gap for criterion=='factuality' findings: G4-W17 arrival item 39 (2026-09-07, Aspose.Cells for Java finding F07 - byte-identical shape: empty fact_ids, empty absent, quote WAS the sentence called missing) made a factuality finding naming NEITHER a fact_id NOR an absent claim stand refuted, with the exact message 'a factuality finding names neither a product fact_id to contradict the quote nor an absent claim of missing text: nothing in evidence supports judging it' (lines 274-280). No equivalent gate exists for criterion=='presentation' - cited_fact_defect() only ever refutes a presentation finding that DOES cite a product fact whose literal value the quote already contains (item 63's fix); it has no branch for a presentation finding that cites nothing at all. F06 falls exactly into that gap: a required-row (scope_limitations, README_CONTRACT.md row 16) presentation finding, corroborated by two independent reads of the SAME shared bias, that names nothing any repair round could act on because repair_packet's records are drawn from the defect's own citations - item 39's own reasoning ('an assertion nothing could ever disprove or fix') applies verbatim, just under a different criterion value.

proposals.defect: A finding whose fact_ids and absent are both empty carries nothing scope_defect's criterion-specific refutations can check. factuality_defect (item 39) already refuses to let such a finding stand for criterion=='factuality'. cited_fact_defect has no equivalent refusal for criterion=='presentation': it simply returns None (finding stands) the moment 'product' is empty (line 352-353), identically to how it stood before item 39 for factuality. absence_defect shares the same early-return shape for the same reason (line 442-443) but is criterion-agnostic and cannot alone close the gap, since a presentation finding routes to cited_fact_defect next regardless.

weakening BC-10 or the two-reader corroboration rule - both are working correctly; corroboration answers 'did two reads agree', never 'is the claim checkable', and this gap is squarely the second question
proposals.reversal_path: Revert the added gate; F06-shaped findings return to standing unconditionally whenever criterion=='presentation' and both citation fields are empty.
